elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: The retained warranties say only that "the Service will perform in all material respects to industry standards" (ii) and that services "shall comply with the terms of this Agreement and shall be free from errors that materially affect their utility" (vi). No "professional and workmanlike manner" performance standard is inserted; a manner-of-performance covenant is different from a performance-to-industry-standards outcome warranty.

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "the Service, the Auction Platform and any deliverables provided hereunder will conform in all material respects to their documentation".

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: The insertion sets "a period of ninety (90) days following delivery" for documentation conformance, not twelve months.
The services warranty is expressly limited to "a period of thirty (30) days following performance", short of the preferred 90 days.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "Customer's remedy ... is, at Kubient's option, repair or replacement of the non-conforming item ...".
Inserted: "... or a refund of the fees paid for it."

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: Retained clause (ix): Kubient "is now and throughout the Term shall comply with all applicable Laws in connection with the operation of its business and the performance of its obligations hereunder or the provision of the Service" (subject to a materiality qualifier).

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: The rationale asserts a no-malicious-code warranty exists among the Kubient representations, but no such wording appears in the cited paragraphs or the rendered operative language (only (ii), (vi), (ix), (x), (xi) and the insertion are shown). Cannot verify from the record supplied.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: Insertion expressly covers the software platform: "for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, the Service, the Auction Platform and any deliverables provided hereunder will conform in all material respects to their documentation" \u2014 an express item-to-documentation warranty for exactly 90 days, not merely a services/output conformance.

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: Insertion: "for a period of thirty (30) days following performance, the services provided hereunder will conform in all material respects to the requirements of this Agreement" \u2014 a stated 30-day services warranty period, which the pre-existing clause (vi) lacked.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: "Customer's remedy for breach of this clause (xii) is, at Kubient's option, repair or replacement of the non-conforming item ..."
"... or a refund of the fees paid for it." Refund is an available remedy at Vendor's election alongside repair/replacement, matching the model language.

reasons: The fallback checklist is complete: 90-day documentation conformance for the Service/Auction Platform/deliverables, a 30-day services warranty, and a repair-or-replacement-or-refund remedy are all in the inserted operative text.

Preferred is not reached: no "professional and workmanlike manner" standard, software period is 90 days rather than 12 months, and the services period is 30 days rather than 90 days. The no-malicious-code element could not be verified from the paragraphs supplied \u2014 if it is not actually present elsewhere in Section (b), the preferred gap is wider than the comment suggests.

Minimality holds: the insertion is a single new sub-clause supplying only the missing conformance periods and remedy; nothing favourable is deleted, the existing warranties (ii), (vi), (ix)\u2013(xi) survive untouched, and the Section 13 disclaimer\u2019s "except for the representations and warranties set forth in this Agreement" carve-out already preserves the new express warranty, so no disclaimer edit was needed.

Intent is preserved: the 30-day services conformance warranty sits alongside, and does not contradict, retained clause (vi) (which is unlimited in time as to compliance with the Agreement and utility-affecting errors); the new clause adds a remedy rather than displacing existing rights.

Drafting repair to make before sending: the remedy sentence refers to "this clause (xii)" but the inserted paragraph as rendered carries no (xii) enumerator following clause (xi). Add the "(xii)" designator (or change the reference to "this clause") so the cross-reference is not dangling.

Optional upgrade ask, consistent with the comment: seek 12 months for the Auction Platform/Service and a "professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards" performance warranty, but the current text is already acceptable at the fallback.
